mainTopic: The סוטה's refusal, the bitter water, the משנה on erasing the scroll and זכות, and רבי מאיר's קנקנתום ink
overview: The גמרא notes that two ברייתות quote רבי עקיבא differently about the last point at which a סוטה can refuse to drink. It answers that two תנאים disagree about his view. It then asks about a woman who calmly refused and later agreed to drink, and that question stays תיקו. אבוה דשמואל rules that something bitter must be put into the water, based on 'מי המרים'. A new משנה explains what happens if she refuses or confesses before or after the scroll is erased. It also describes how a guilty woman is struck, and how זכות can delay her punishment. This leads to the מחלוקת between בן עזאי and רבי אליעזר about teaching a daughter תורה, and to רבי יהושע's sayings. The גמרא then tells רבי מאיר's story about putting קנקנתום in his ink and רבי ישמעאל's warning that the סוטה's writing must be erasable. Two reports of the story clash: the order of his teachers is reconciled, but who forbade the ink stays a קשיא. Finally, a ברייתא begins quoting רבי מאיר's general permission to use קנקנתום, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two statements of רבי עקיבא seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי עקיבא gives two different cut-off points for when a סוטה can no longer refuse to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a contradiction between one statement of רבי עקיבא and another. There he said the erasing of the scroll is what stops her from backing out, and here he says the קומץ is what stops her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets one ברייתא against another. Both quote רבי עקיבא, but they give different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In one ברייתא, רבי עקיבא says that once the scroll is erased into the water, she can no longer refuse. If she refuses after that, she is made to drink. In the other ברייתא, he says the deadline is the offering of the קומץ from her מנחה. One person cannot hold both deadlines, so the גמרא asks which one he really held.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty or contradiction
Erasing the scroll with the curses into the water
The handful of flour taken from the סוטה's מנחה and burned on the מזבח
Holds back or prevents; here, it marks the point after which she cannot back out

phrases.english: There is a contradiction between Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Akiva:
There he said the erasing is what prevents her from backing out,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the first ברייתא quoted earlier.

phrases.english: and here he says the handful is what prevents her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares two ברייתות quoted earlier on the דף
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי עקיבא's position
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא puts the deadline at the erasing of the scroll, and the other puts it at the קומץ. One person cannot hold both.

steps.title: Two תנאים disagree about what רבי עקיבא held
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction is resolved by saying that the two ברייתות reflect two different reports of רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two תנאים, and they disagree about what רבי עקיבא held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. רבי עקיבא himself did not say two things. Two later תנאים reported his opinion differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not try to make the two ברייתות agree. It accepts that they disagree. The disagreement is between the students who passed on his opinion, not inside רבי עקיבא's own view.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים who disagree
According to the view of

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבי עקיבא changed his mind. It means two תנאים quoted him differently.

phrases.english: It is two tanna'im, and they disagree about Rabbi Akiva's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different reports of one תנא's view (תרי תנאי אליבא דרבי עקיבא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות give רבי עקיבא's own single view, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא follows a different תנא's report of רבי עקיבא's view.

steps.title: She refused to drink, then agreed: what is the law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a woman who said 'I will not drink' while calm and later said 'I will drink'. It lays out both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if she said 'I will not drink' while she was well, and then changed her mind and said 'I will drink', what is the law? Maybe saying 'I will not drink' is like saying 'I am טמאה'. Since she has treated herself as טמאה, she cannot take it back. Or maybe, since she now says 'I will drink', she has shown that she only refused out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question, an איבעיא. It then shows the two ways it could go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: refusing to drink counts as a confession. Once she has made herself טמאה, she cannot take it back. Side two: her later agreement shows that the refusal was not a real confession, only fear of the bitter water. So she may still drink.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים
Health; a calm, healthy state
She treated herself as טמאה
Go back on what she said
Fear, fright

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:
If she said 'I will not drink' while she was well,
and then went back and said 'I will drink', what is the law?
Since she said 'I will not drink',
she is in effect saying 'I am defiled',
and since she has treated herself as defiled,
she cannot go back on it.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא כֵּיוָן דְּאָמְרָה שׁוֹתָה אֲנִי —
phrases.english: Or perhaps, since she said 'I will drink',

phrases.aramaic: גַּלִּיָא דַּעְתַּהּ דְּמֵחֲמַת בִּיעֲתוּתָא הוּא דְּאָמְרָה.
phrases.english: she has shown that she only said it out of fear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about a woman who refuses and then changes her mind
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a calm refusal to drink a binding confession of טומאה, or can she take it back because it may have been only fear?

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the question with תיקו: it stays undecided.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot find a source that decides the question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means neither side was proven. The law in this case stays a ספק, an undecided doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: If she refused to drink while calm and then agreed, we do not know whether she may still drink. The question is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the איבעיא from step 3 without an answer

steps.title: Something bitter must be put into the water
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל rules that a bitter substance must be added to the סוטה's water.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father of שמואל said: one must put something bitter into the water.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule is stated. Something bitter has to be put into the סוטה's water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic: how the water is prepared. The water must actually be bitter, not just called 'bitter water'.

keyTerms.meaning: The father of the אמורא שמואל
Something bitter

phrases.english: Shmuel's father said:
One must put something bitter into the water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how the water is prepared
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bitter substance must be added to the סוטה's water.

steps.title: The source: 'the bitter water' is bitter already
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק 'מי המרים' as the source for adding something bitter.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the פסוק says 'the bitter water', meaning it is bitter already.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of אבוה דשמואל's rule and finds it in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls it 'bitter water' at the point when the scroll is erased into it. So the water must already be bitter before the erasing. Plain water is not bitter, so something bitter has to be added.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Because the פסוק says
The bitter water

steps.whatToRemember: The water is already bitter before the scroll is erased into it. That is why something bitter is added.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the verse says: 'the water of bitterness',
meaning it is bitter already.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule in step 5
steps.raayaObject: The rule that something bitter must be added to the water
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'ומחה אל מי המרים' (במדבר 5:23) calls the water bitter before the erasing.

steps.title: Refusing or confessing before or after the scroll is erased
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives three cases: she refuses before the scroll is erased, she confesses after it is erased, or she refuses after it is erased.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she says 'I will not drink' before the scroll is erased, the scroll is put away, her מנחה is scattered on the ashes, and the scroll cannot be used for another סוטה. If the scroll was erased and she says 'I am impure,' the water is poured out and her מנחה is scattered on the place of the ashes. If the scroll was erased and she says 'I will not drink,' they force her mouth open and make her drink against her will.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains what happens if the סוטה backs out or admits guilt, and the answer depends on whether the scroll was already erased into the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the erasing, she may still refuse, and the process simply stops. Once the scroll with its writing has been erased into the water, refusal no longer helps and she is made to drink. If she confesses, though, she is no longer a doubtful case, so the water is poured out.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
The scroll was erased (dissolved into the water)
Is put away and hidden, not thrown out
The place where the ashes are dumped
They force her mouth open
Against her will

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two 'after erasing' cases. If she says 'I am impure,' she does not drink at all. Only if she says 'I won't drink' is she forced to drink.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Before the scroll was erased
she said: "I will not drink"
her scroll is put away
and her meal-offering is scattered over the ashes
and her scroll is not fit
to make another סוטה drink with it
If the scroll was erased and she said: "I am impure"
the water is poured out
and her meal-offering is scattered on the place of the ashes
If the scroll was erased and she said: "I will not drink"
they force her mouth open
and make her drink against her will

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous גמרא discussion about adding a bitter substance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before erasing, she may refuse. After erasing, confession cancels the drinking, but plain refusal does not, and she is made to drink.

steps.title: What happens to a guilty woman when she drinks
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the immediate signs of punishment and the rush to take her out of the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: She does not even finish drinking before her face turns green, her eyes bulge, and she swells with veins. The people say: 'Take her out, take her out, so she does not make the עזרה impure!'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes what happens to a guilty סוטה after she drinks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment hits fast and is visible to everyone. The onlookers rush her out because if she dies inside, her body would make the עזרה impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Turn green or pale
Bulge out
Veins
The courtyard of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: She does not manage to finish drinking
before her face turns green
and her eyes bulge
and she becomes full of veins
and they say: Take her out, take her out
phrases.notes: The second 'take her out' is the one in square brackets. Some versions say it twice.

phrases.english: so that she does not make the Temple courtyard impure
phrases.notes: If she died there, her body would make the courtyard impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה: after she drinks, here is what happens if she is guilty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A guilty סוטה is struck at once, and she is taken out so she does not make the עזרה impure.

steps.title: Merit can delay her punishment
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits the previous statement: a guilty woman with זכות may not die right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she has merit, it holds off the punishment. Some merit holds it off one year, some two years, and some three years.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a limit to what it just said. A guilty woman will not always be punished immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step sounded like a guilty woman always dies on the spot. Now we learn that her זכות can delay the punishment by one, two, or three years, depending on how great it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Merit from good deeds or מצוות
Holds off; literally 'hangs,' meaning it suspends the punishment

steps.confusionAlert: The זכות does not mean she is innocent. It only delays the punishment of a woman who is guilty.

phrases.english: If she has merit
it would hold off the punishment for her
There is merit that holds it off one year
there is merit that holds it off two years
there is merit that holds it off three years

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם יֵשׁ לָהּ זְכוּת הָיְתָה תּוֹלָה לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the previous step: immediate punishment is not universal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זכות can delay a guilty סוטה's punishment by up to three years.

steps.title: בן עזאי: a father must teach his daughter Torah
steps.stepSummary: From the rule about זכות, בן עזאי concludes that a father must teach his daughter תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here בן עזאי says: A person must teach his daughter תורה, so that if she drinks and is not punished right away, she will know that זכות is holding off the punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי draws a practical lesson from the rule that זכות delays punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a guilty woman drinks and nothing happens right away, she might think the waters do not work. Knowing תורה, she will understand that her זכות is only delaying the punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: From here; a conclusion drawn from what was just said
A תנא
Obligated

phrases.english: From here בן עזאי says

phrases.aramaic: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְלַמֵּד אֶת בִּתּוֹ תּוֹרָה
phrases.english: A person is obligated to teach his daughter Torah
so that if she drinks
she will know that merit is holding off the punishment for her

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical conclusion from the rule that זכות delays punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father must teach his daughter תורה so she understands that a delay in punishment comes from זכות.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר disagrees about teaching daughters Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that teaching a daughter תורה is like teaching her תפלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Anyone who teaches his daughter תורה is teaching her תפלות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives the opposite view to בן עזאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי sees teaching a daughter תורה as protection. רבי אליעזר sees it as harmful and compares it to teaching her תפלות. The משנה does not explain his reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: Promiscuity or foolishness; something improper
A תנא who argues on בן עזאי here

steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת: בן עזאי obligates teaching one's daughter תורה, and רבי אליעזר opposes it.

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says
Anyone who teaches his daughter Torah
(it is as if) he teaches her promiscuity
phrases.notes: Some versions have the round-bracket words 'as if' and some leave them out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר כׇּל הַמְלַמֵּד בִּתּוֹ תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposing opinion to בן עזאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching a daughter תורה is like teaching her תפלות.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: a woman prefers a little with closeness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says a woman prefers one קב of food with תפלות over nine קבין with פרישות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: A woman would rather have one קב of food with closeness to her husband than nine קבין with separation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a saying of רבי יהושע that uses the same word, תפלות, as רבי אליעזר did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here תפלות means a married relationship. רבי יהושע says a woman values that relationship more than having plenty while living apart. The משנה itself does not spell out how this connects to רבי אליעזר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of food
Separation; holding back from a married relationship
A תנא

phrases.english: רבי יהושע says
A woman prefers one kav of food with intimacy
phrases.notes: Here תפלות means closeness with her husband, not something wrong.

phrases.english: over nine kav with separation

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר רוֹצָה אִשָּׁה בְּקַב וְתִפְלוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related saying linked by the word תפלות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman prefers a little along with a married relationship over plenty with separation.

steps.title: People who destroy the world
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע lists four kinds of people whose false or foolish piety destroys the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: He used to say: A foolish pious man, a cunning wicked man, a woman who acts overly separate, and those who hurt themselves out of false פרישות all destroy the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with another saying of רבי יהושע. He warns against piety that is foolish or fake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person on the list causes damage to the world. The foolish חסיד means well but acts badly. The cunning רשע does harm through scheming, and the falsely separate people make a show of holding back. The משנה lists them but does not explain each one here.

keyTerms.meaning: A foolish pious person
A cunning, scheming wicked person
Blows of the falsely separate, who hurt themselves to look pious
Destroyers of the world

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה moves from the laws of the סוטה to a broader warning. Piety without wisdom or honesty causes harm.

phrases.english: He used to say
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהושע, from the previous line.

phrases.english: a foolish pious man
and a cunning wicked man
and a woman who is overly separate
and the blows of the falsely separate
these all destroy the world

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further saying of the same תנא, closing the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Foolish or false piety destroys the world.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל warns the scribe רבי מאיר to be careful with every letter
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר tells how רבי עקיבא let his ink practice pass, while רבי ישמעאל warned him that one missing or extra letter could destroy the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: When I learned with רבי עקיבא, I put iron sulfate in my ink and he said nothing. When I came to רבי ישמעאל, he asked what my job was. I said I was a scribe. He told me: Be careful! Your work is holy work. If you leave out or add even one letter, you could destroy the whole world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a story from רבי מאיר about his work as a scribe. It sets up the main discussion about the ink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two teachers react to the same scribe in different ways. רבי עקיבא's silence means he did not object to the קנקנתום. רבי ישמעאל stresses that writing a ספר תורה is so delicate that one wrong letter can change the meaning of a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Iron sulfate, which makes ink dark and hard to erase
Ink
A scribe who writes holy scrolls
Work for Heaven; holy work

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously חז"ל treated the exact letters of the תורה.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says
in the name of Rabbi Meir:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהָיִיתִי לָמֵד תּוֹרָה אֵצֶל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: When I was studying Torah with Rabbi Akiva,
I used to put iron sulfate into the ink,
and he did not say anything to me.
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא's silence tells us he had no problem with it.

phrases.english: When I came to Rabbi Yishmael,
he said to me: My son, what is your work?
I said to him: I am a scribe.
He said to me: My son, be careful,
for your work is the work of Heaven,
lest you leave out one letter
or add one letter,

phrases.aramaic: נִמְצֵאתָ אַתָּה מַחְרִיב אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ.
phrases.english: and you are found destroying the entire world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion with a story about scribal ink and care with letters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scribe must be very careful, since one wrong letter can ruin the meaning of the תורה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל objects that the ink must be erasable
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר mentions his קנקנתום, and רבי ישמעאל objects: the תורה says "וּמָחָה", so the writing must be erasable.
steps.simpleTranslation: I told him: I have something I put in the ink, called iron sulfate. He said to me: You may put iron sulfate in ink? The תורה says "and he shall blot it out." That means writing that can be blotted out!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר mentions the special ink, and רבי ישמעאל challenges it from a פסוק about the סוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סוטה ritual the curses are written and then rubbed off into the water. Ink with קנקנתום does not come off, so רבי ישמעאל says it cannot be used. For now, רבי מאיר's reply seems to have nothing to do with the warning about letters.

keyTerms.meaning: "And he shall blot out" (said about the סוטה's scroll)
Writing that can be erased
"And is it really so?" (a surprised question)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: דָּבָר אֶחָד יֵשׁ לִי
phrases.english: I said to him: I have one thing
that I put into the ink,
and its name is iron sulfate.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: וְכִי מְטִילִין קַנְקַנְתּוֹם לְתוֹךְ הַדְּיוֹ?
phrases.english: He said to me: May one put iron sulfate into the ink?
The Torah said "and he shall blot out,"
writing that can be blotted out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story. רבי מאיר's ink practice draws an objection from רבי ישמעאל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's use of קנקנתום in his ink
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah requires the סוטה's writing to be erasable ("וּמָחָה"), and קנקנתום makes ink impossible to erase.

steps.title: How does רבי מאיר's answer fit רבי ישמעאל's warning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the conversation hangs together, since mentioning the ink seems unrelated to the warning about letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was he saying to him, and what was he answering him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops the story to ask a question. It is setting up an explanation of how רבי מאיר's reply connects to the warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל warned about adding or leaving out letters. רבי מאיר answered about his ink, which seems to have nothing to do with it. The גמרא wants to know the logic behind the exchange.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying to him?
Answers or replies

phrases.english: What is he saying to him
phrases.notes: First, what was רבי ישמעאל saying to רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: and what is he answering him?
phrases.notes: Next, what was רבי מאיר's reply.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ וּמַאי קָא מַהְדַּר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how רבי מאיר's reply in the story connects to the warning before it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The link between the warning about letters and the reply about קנקנתום.

steps.title: רבי מאיר meant his ink protects even against a fly erasing a letter
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר was saying that he is so careful that his ink cannot even be smudged by a fly turning a ד into a ר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: Of course I am an expert in missing and extra letters. I even worry that a fly might land on the corner of a ד, rub it off, and turn it into a ר. That is why I have something I put in the ink, called iron sulfate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the exchange. רבי מאיר was telling רבי ישמעאל how careful he already is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's answer was not off topic. He meant: you warn me about letters, but I go even further and protect letters from being changed by accident. The קנקנתום keeps the corner of the ד from rubbing off, so it can never look like a ר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not even necessary to say (this is obvious)
Expert
A fly
The corner or crown sticking out at the top of a letter

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר used קנקנתום so his letters could never be changed by accident. רבי ישמעאל objected because the סוטה's scroll must be erasable ("וּמָחָה").
steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not changing the subject. His ink point is his proof that he takes the warning about letters very seriously.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying to him:
Not only with missing and extra letters
am I an expert,
but even regarding worry about a fly
that maybe it comes and sits
on the corner of the dalet
and erases it and turns it into a reish

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר אֶחָד יֵשׁ לִי שֶׁאֲנִי מֵטִיל לְתוֹךְ הַדְּיוֹ
phrases.english: I have one thing that I put into the ink
and its name is iron sulfate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 by explaining רבי מאיר's reply.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר was showing that he takes extra care. His קנקנתום keeps a fly from smudging a ד into a ר.

steps.title: A ברייתא tells the ink story the other way around
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's report with a ברייתא. In it, רבי ישמעאל says nothing about the ink and רבי עקיבא forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? A ברייתא teaches that רבי מאיר said: 'When I learned with רבי ישמעאל, I put קנקנתום in my ink and he said nothing. When I came to רבי עקיבא, he forbade it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the story we just learned about רבי מאיר and his ink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב יהודה's version, רבי עקיבא came first and said nothing, and רבי ישמעאל came later and forbade the ink. In the ברייתא it is the reverse: רבי ישמעאל came first and stayed silent, and רבי עקיבא came later and forbade it. Both the order of the teachers and the identity of the one who forbade it are flipped.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? This word opens a challenge.
But isn't it taught (in a ברייתא)?
Iron sulfate, a chemical that makes ink dark and hard to erase
Ink
He forbade it to me

phrases.english: Is that so?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהָיִיתִי לָמֵד תּוֹרָה אֵצֶל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
phrases.english: When I was learning Torah with Rabbi Yishmael,
I used to put iron sulfate into the ink,
and he did not say anything to me.
When I came to Rabbi Akiva,
he forbade it to me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual account of the story told in steps 14-15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's report about the order of רבי מאיר's teachers and about who forbade the קנקנתום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא gives the reverse account, so both reports cannot be true as they stand.

steps.title: Splitting the clash into two separate contradictions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that there are really two problems. One is about which teacher came first. The other is about which teacher forbade the ink.
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'serving' in one report contradicts the 'serving' in the other. And the 'forbidding' in one contradicts the 'forbidding' in the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the two separate contradictions so it can deal with each one on its own. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first problem is about which teacher רבי מאיר served first. The second is about who forbade the קנקנתום. Separating them lets the גמרא answer one even if it cannot answer the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Serving a teacher as his student
X contradicts Y (the letter אַ means 'against')

phrases.english: Serving contradicts serving.
phrases.notes: The two reports disagree about which teacher רבי מאיר studied under first.

phrases.english: Forbidding contradicts forbidding!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks the challenge of step 18 into two separate parts.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both parts of רב יהודה's account: the order of the teachers and who forbade the ink.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each detail is directly reversed in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי מאיר went to רבי עקיבא, then to רבי ישמעאל, then back to רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The order of the teachers is not a real contradiction. רבי מאיר started with רבי עקיבא, moved to רבי ישמעאל, and later returned to רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The serving contradiction is no problem. At first he went to רבי עקיבא. Since he could not follow his reasoning, he went to רבי ישמעאל and learned the basic material. Then he went back to רבי עקיבא and learned the reasoning behind it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the first contradiction by showing that both reports are true: רבי מאיר studied with רבי עקיבא twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's report describes רבי מאיר's first time with רבי עקיבא. The ברייתא describes his time with רבי ישמעאל and then his return to רבי עקיבא. Once there are three stages, the two 'orders' fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part works. It usually means another part does not.
At first
To grasp his way of thinking
Learned the received material, the basic tradition
Studied the reasoning behind the material

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a classic model of learning: first master the basic material, then go deep into the reasoning.

phrases.english: Granted, serving against serving is not difficult:
At first he came before Rabbi Akiva.
Since he could not grasp his reasoning,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, and the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: he came before Rabbi Yishmael,
and learned the tradition.
Then he came back before Rabbi Akiva
and studied the reasoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first of the two contradictions named in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonizing the two reports by adding a third stage to the timeline
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר studied with each teacher only once, so the two reports cannot both be right.
steps.terutzMaskana: He studied with רבי עקיבא twice, before and after רבי ישמעאל, so both reports are correct.

steps.title: The question of who forbade the ink stays unsolved
steps.stepSummary: The second contradiction, about who forbade the קנקנתום, has no answer. The גמרא leaves it as קשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the forbidding contradiction is still difficult! Indeed, it is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it cannot settle whether רבי ישמעאל or רבי עקיבא forbade the ink, and it ends with קשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The timeline answer fixes the order of the teachers. It does not explain why each report names a different teacher as the one who forbade the ink. The question is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: But, however. Here it shows the other part is still a problem.

steps.confusionAlert: Ending with 'קַשְׁיָא' means the question was left open without an answer. It does not mean a statement was disproved; that would be תְּיוּבְתָּא.
steps.whatToRemember: The order of רבי מאיר's teachers is explained (רבי עקיבא, then רבי ישמעאל, then רבי עקיבא again). Who forbade the קנקנתום stays an open question.

phrases.english: But forbidding against forbidding is difficult!
It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the second contradiction from step 19, which step 20 did not answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The contradiction about who forbade the קנקנתום is left unresolved (קשיא).

steps.title: רבי מאיר allows קנקנתום in ink for all writings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה reporting that רבי מאיר said קנקנתום may be put into the ink for everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says that רבי מאיר used to say, "For everything, we may put קנקנתום into the ink."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא where רבי מאיר gives a general rule allowing קנקנתום in ink. The sentence is only starting here, and it sets up an exception that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier sources were about whether קנקנתום was allowed at all. This ברייתא gives רבי מאיר's rule as a broad permission ("for everything"). The word "everything" suggests a limit or exception is about to follow.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was taught." This introduces a ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that is outside the משנה.
A chemical (iron sulfate) added to ink to make it dark and very hard to erase.
Ink.
"We put in" or "we add."
"For everything." Here it means all holy writings.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says,
Rabbi Meir used to say:
For everything, we may put iron sulfate
phrases.notes: "Everything" means all holy writings, like a ספר תורה, תפילין and מזוזות. Watch for the exception coming next.

phrases.english: into the ink,

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the unresolved contradiction in step 21, the גמרא brings a new ברייתא that gives רבי מאיר's own rule about קנקנתום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, as reported by רבי יהודה, קנקנתום may generally be added to ink for all holy writings. An exception is about to follow.
